title: 2015-09 — Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
disposition_detail: The SJC found the BCO 40-5 Request/Application administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order under OMSJC 9.1.a., and dismissed the case under OMSJC 9.2(d); it made no merits ruling on the underlying deposition/censure.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed a BCO 40-5 application by Brad Bumgarner against Mississippi Valley Presbytery because the matter concerned proceedings in a judicial case and the claimant had withdrawn an earlier complaint. The concurring opinion explained that the application was out of order as an attempt to refile a withdrawn complaint and to reverse a censure through BCO 40.
summary: A claimant sought BCO 40-5 review of Presbytery’s handling of his earlier judicial case, alleging grossly unconstitutional proceedings and delinquency in failing to investigate his 2012 deposition. The SJC found the application administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 40-3 excludes judicial-case proceedings from review and control when notice of appeal or complaint has been given, and he had withdrawn his 2012 complaint acknowledging it could not be resubmitted. It dismissed under OMSJC 9.2(d). The concurrence added that BCO 40 cannot refile a withdrawn complaint or reverse a censure.
